standard_prerequisites.name: Signed-formula reading of tableaux derivability
standard_prerequisites.statement: Gamma proves B iff for some finite list C_1,...,C_n from Gamma the signed assumption set {False B, True C_1, ..., True C_n} has a closed tableau.
standard_prerequisites.use: Both hypotheses are unpacked into closed-tableau existence for finite signed assumption sets.

standard_prerequisites.name: The Cut rule
standard_prerequisites.statement: A tableau branch may be split on any sentence A into a branch with True A and one with False A.
standard_prerequisites.use: The composition step: Cut on A yields two branches, each carrying exactly the assumptions of one of the two given closed tableaux.

core_obligations: Statement (lines 694-698): if Gamma proves A and {A} union Delta proves B, then Gamma union Delta proves B.

Unpacking (proof lines 700-712): {A} union Delta proves B gives a finite Delta_0 = {C_1,...,C_n} with {False B, True A, True C_1,...,True C_n} closed; Gamma proves A gives D_1,...,D_m in Gamma with {False A, True D_1,...,True D_m} closed.

Cut composition (proof lines 714-741): build the tableau with assumptions {False B, True C_1,...,True C_n, True D_1,...,True D_m} and apply Cut on A; the True-A branch carries exactly the first assumption set, so attaching the first closed tableau closes every branch through it; the False-A branch carries the second set and closes likewise; hence Gamma union Delta proves B.
proof_roadmap: Unpack both derivability hypotheses into finite closed-tableau witnesses.
Combine the finite assumption lists and split on A by Cut.
Attach the two existing closed tableaux to the two branches.
